title: In one mouse retina patch, ganglion-cell ON/OFF polarity follows dendrite stratification inside types, but this explains only 4% of reliable within-type variation; kinetics show no such link
abstract: Question: in the e2198 mouse retina patch, does the inner plexiform layer (IPL) stratification of a ganglion cell predict its moving-bar calcium response only through its type, or also inside a type? Data: Briggman 2011 calcium responses and Bae 2018 EM reconstructions of the same cells (299 typed cells in 37 types for ON/OFF, 288 in 36 types for kinetics). Method: fraction of dendrite volume in the ON layer (f_on) and in the central band; ON/OFF index and decay from the source fits; between-type slope versus within-type slope with type and imaging-field fixed effects; within-type permutations; a fixed decision rule written before outcomes. Results: between types, f_on predicted the ON/OFF index (slope 1.30, r 0.77). Within types, the slope was 0.88 (95% interval 0.14-1.43; Holm p 0.005; ratio to between slope 0.68, 0.11-1.10), also outside the direction-selective types, and positive in 20 of 26 types. But f_on varies little inside types, and it explained about 4% of within-type ON/OFF variance, while that variance was 93% reliable across repeats. Without two atypical high-leverage cells the slope was 0.53 (p 0.067). The pre-set kinetics measure failed a sign check; the source sustainedness index showed the type-level rule (r -0.47) but no within-type link, with low reliability (0.52). Limitations: one animal, one stimulus, parametric fits, unestimated stratification error.

display.caption: A: type means of the ON/OFF index against ON-layer dendrite fraction (between-type slope 1.30). B: within-type deviations after type and field effects (slope 0.88; dashed line = between-type slope). C: within-type correlation for each type with at least 5 cells.

A: between-type and within-type slopes with bootstrap intervals for the ON/OFF test (P1), the pre-set kinetics test (P2) and the exploratory sustainedness test (E1). B: reliable within-type variance (split-half) and the part explained by stratification.
